# CINE-DNA — Camera / Film / Lens recognition skill

> Machine-facing reference. Injected into the LLM context for the Image Analyzer
> "Analyse Style" call (and reusable by Realism Forge, BZ Camera Suite, Image DNA).
> Purpose: let the model estimate the SHOOTING ORIGIN of an image (camera, sensor/
> film, lens, lighting, grade) precisely, and verbalize it as a ready-to-use prompt
> fragment in ENGLISH. Keep concise; extend over time.

---

## 0. First decision — is it a photograph?

Before estimating any camera spec, decide if the image is a real photograph/film
capture or NOT (illustration, 2D cartoon, anime/cel, 3D render, painting, comic,
vector, pixel art, AI-stylized).

- If NON-photographic → DO NOT invent camera/film/lens specs. Output only the medium
  and rendering style (e.g. `2D cel-shaded anime`, `clean-line cartoon`, `stylized 3D
  render`, `oil painting`, `flat vector illustration`), and state camera info is N/A.
- If photographic → proceed with full estimation below.

Photographic tells: real optical depth of field & focus falloff, lens distortion,
sensor/film grain, specular highlights on real materials, motion blur, chromatic
aberration, rolling-shutter, vignetting, real-world lighting imperfections.

---

## 1. Capture era / device signatures

| Look | Tells | Verbalize as |
|---|---|---|
| Modern digital cinema | clean, high DR, controlled grain, filmic grade | `digital cinema camera (ARRI Alexa-class), clean highlights, wide dynamic range` |
| Modern smartphone | deep DoF, computational HDR, slight over-sharpening, wide-angle | `smartphone capture, deep focus, HDR computational look` |
| DSLR/mirrorless photo | shallow DoF possible, crisp, neutral | `full-frame DSLR/mirrorless, sharp, shallow depth of field` |
| 35mm film | organic grain, halation on highlights, gentle roll-off | `35mm film, fine grain, halation, soft highlight roll-off` |
| 16mm film | heavier grain, slightly soft, vintage doc feel | `16mm film, pronounced grain, documentary texture` |
| Super 8 / home movie | heavy grain, gate weave, warm fade, low res | `Super 8, heavy grain, gate weave, faded warm tones` |
| Polaroid / instant | soft, low contrast, color shift, white frame | `instant film (Polaroid), soft, milky contrast, pastel shift` |
| Disposable / point-and-shoot | flash falloff, vignetting, date stamp vibe | `disposable camera, direct flash, vignetting, 90s snapshot` |
| Camcorder / MiniDV | interlacing, low DR, video sharpening, 4:3 | `MiniDV camcorder, video look, interlaced, low dynamic range` |
| VHS | scanlines, chroma bleed, tracking noise | `VHS, scanlines, chroma bleed, tape noise` |
| Webcam / surveillance | low-res, fixed wide lens, noise, timestamp | `surveillance/webcam, low resolution, fixed wide lens, sensor noise` |
| Early photography | sepia, soft, plate look | `early 20th-century plate photography, sepia, soft focus` |

---

## 2. Sensor / format

- Full-frame (35mm) — shallow DoF for a given framing; the default cinema/photo look.
- Medium format — extreme detail, smooth tonal transitions, gentle DoF: `medium format, ultra-detailed, smooth tonality`.
- APS-C / crop — slightly deeper DoF.
- Anamorphic — 2.39:1 framing, oval bokeh, horizontal blue flares, edge stretch: `anamorphic, oval bokeh, horizontal lens flares, 2.39:1`.

---

## 3. Film stocks (color signatures to recognize)

- Kodak Portra — warm, soft pastel skin, low contrast: `Kodak Portra, warm pastel skin tones`.
- Kodak Vision3 (cine) — neutral filmic, clean shadows: `Kodak Vision3 cinema stock`.
- Kodak Ektar — saturated, fine grain.
- CineStill 800T — tungsten-balanced, red halation around lights, night look: `CineStill 800T, red halation, tungsten night`.
- Fuji (Pro 400H / Eterna) — green-leaning, airy, soft: `Fujifilm, cool green cast, airy`.
- Ektachrome / slide — punchy, contrasty, vivid blues.
- B&W: Tri-X (gritty grain, high contrast), HP5 (classic doc), T-Max (fine grain): `Tri-X black and white, gritty grain, high contrast`.

---

## 4. Lens / focal length (read from perspective & compression)

- Ultra-wide (14-24mm) — strong perspective, edge distortion, expansive: `ultra-wide 16mm, deep perspective, slight edge distortion`.
- Wide (28-35mm) — environmental, mild distortion: `35mm wide, environmental framing`.
- Normal (40-55mm) — natural perspective, human-eye: `50mm, natural perspective`.
- Short tele / portrait (85-135mm) — compression, flattering, creamy bokeh: `85mm portrait, compressed, creamy bokeh`.
- Tele (200mm+) — strong compression, isolated subject, shallow plane.
- Macro — extreme close detail, razor-thin focus.
- Vintage glass — lower contrast, swirly/soap-bubble bokeh, flares: `vintage lens, low-contrast, swirly bokeh, blooming flares`.
- Tilt-shift / miniature — selective focus plane, toy-like.

Recognition cues: facial feature compression (tele) vs nose-forward distortion (wide);
background size relative to subject; bokeh shape/size; falloff steepness.

---

## 5. Aperture / depth of field

- Wide open (f/1.2-2) — razor-thin focus, large soft bokeh: `f/1.4, very shallow depth of field, large bokeh`.
- Mid (f/2.8-5.6) — subject pop with readable background.
- Stopped down (f/8-16) — deep focus, everything sharp: `f/11, deep focus`.

---

## 6. Lighting

Name the scheme + quality + direction + time:
- Schemes: Rembrandt, butterfly, split, rim/back-lit, top, high-key, low-key, motivated/practical.
- Quality: hard (sharp shadows) vs soft (diffused, wrapping).
- Direction: front / side / 3-4 / back / top / under.
- Source: natural (golden hour, overcast, harsh noon, blue hour, window) vs artificial
  (tungsten, neon, fluorescent, hard flash, firelight, screen glow).
Verbalize e.g.: `low-key side lighting, hard shadows, single tungsten source`.

---

## 7. Grain / texture / color grade

- Grain: clean / fine / pronounced / heavy; digital noise vs film grain.
- Halation & bloom on highlights (film tell).
- Color grade: teal-orange blockbuster, bleach bypass (desaturated high-contrast),
  warm vintage, cold desaturated, high-saturation, muted pastel, monochrome.
- Vignetting, chromatic aberration, flares, light leaks.

---

## 8. OUTPUT CONTRACT (how to answer)

- Language: **ENGLISH**.
- Form: a **ready-to-use prompt fragment** — concise, comma-separated descriptors a
  user can paste directly into an image/video prompt (NOT prose, NOT bullet lists,
  NOT explanations).
- Order: camera/era, sensor/format, film/stock or sensor, lens & focal, aperture/DoF,
  lighting, grain/texture, color grade.
- End with: `Style: <one short phrase>` describing the overall look.
- Be specific but only as confident as the pixels justify; prefer concrete named
  references (e.g. "Kodak Portra", "85mm", "anamorphic") over vague terms.
- Non-photographic image → output only medium + rendering style, e.g.:
  `2D cel-shaded anime, clean line art, flat lighting. Style: Studio-anime cartoon. (Camera specs: N/A — non-photographic)`.

Example (photographic):
`35mm film, full-frame, Kodak Portra, 85mm lens, f/2, shallow depth of field, soft
window side-light, fine grain with subtle halation, warm low-contrast grade. Style:
intimate analog portrait.`
